item.title: Consistency Models, CAP, PACELC and Consensus
item.description:
Simple definition#

A consistency model is a promise about what a read can return after writes, when data is copied across machines. Strong models behave like a single copy. Weaker models allow stale or reordered reads in exchange for latency and availability.

item.title: Distributed Transactions: 2PC, XA and the Alternatives
item.description:
Simple definition#

A distributed transaction is an all-or-nothing update that spans more than one database or resource, for example debiting an account in one service and creating a shipment in another.

The problem#

item.title: Transactional Outbox, CDC and Idempotent Consumers
item.description:
Simple definition#

  • Transactional outbox: write the business change and the event to the same database in one transaction, then publish the event from the database to the broker.
  • Change data capture (CDC): read a database’s transaction log and stream every change as events.
  • Idempotent consumer: a consumer that gives the same result whether a message arrives once or several times.

Together they give effectively-once processing without distributed transactions.

item.title: The Saga Pattern
item.description:
Simple definition#

A saga is a sequence of local transactions, one per service. If a step fails, the saga runs compensating transactions to semantically undo the steps that already succeeded. It replaces one big distributed transaction with steps that are each atomic, plus an explicit undo plan.

item.title: CQRS and Event Sourcing
item.description:
Simple definition#

  • CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation): use one model to change data (commands) and one or more different models to read it (queries).
  • Event sourcing: store every change as an immutable event, and derive current state by replaying them, instead of storing only the latest state.

They are often used together, but each works without the other.

item.title: System Design: Order Processing Across Microservices
item.description:
The design brief#

“Customers buy products online. An order must reserve stock, take payment and book delivery. Customers track their order in real time. Peak is 2,000 orders per second during sales. We must never charge for an order we cannot fulfil, and never ship an unpaid order.”
